documents.title: Canonical architecture artifacts
documents.body: Markdown, YAML, and JSON files remain the portable source of truth. Retrieval indexes are derived copies that can be discarded and rebuilt without changing accepted decisions.

documents.title: Codex hook lifecycle
documents.body: Git BBQ installs UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostCompact, and Stop. An invalid workspace or hook configuration fails closed with an explicit denial.

documents.title: Additive legacy migration
documents.body: Approved migration preserves the legacy ai-architect tree, converts validated decisions into docs/adr, archives incompatible Git habits, and does not overwrite pre-existing projection conflicts.

documents.title: Ownership-aware uninstall
documents.body: The ownership ledger records generated-file hashes. Uninstall removes only unchanged regular files, while modified, missing, symlinked, reparse-point, and unowned paths remain preserved.

documents.title: SQLite FTS5 retrieval baseline
documents.body: SQLite FTS5 provides a local keyword retrieval baseline over title and body fields. The index is disposable, rebuildable, and separate from canonical architecture documents.

documents.title: Vector retrieval decision gate
documents.body: Do not add sqlite-vec or external embeddings until representative project questions show a material ranking improvement over FTS5 that justifies dependency, rebuild, backup, and packaging costs.

documents.title: Approved Git operations
documents.body: Git habits describe preferences, but planning and execution remain separate. Commit, tag, push, and remote actions require explicit approval and validated commands.

documents.title: Bounded static inspection
documents.body: Repository analysis treats project files as untrusted data. It reads bounded allowlisted text and never imports, executes, compiles, or tests analyzed application code.

documents.title: Derived index recovery
documents.body: A retrieval database is derived state. Corruption or a missing index is detected, discarded, and recovered by rebuilding from the canonical document set.

documents.title: Cross-platform generated paths
documents.body: Generated paths must remain safe on Windows and Unix. Reparse-point, symlink, traversal, and non-regular path behavior is validated before writes or cleanup.

documents.title: Semantic source vocabulary
documents.body: CONTEXT.md, CONTEXT-MAP.md, and docs/adr provide vocabulary and decision history. Git BBQ projections must not create a second competing architecture history.

documents.title: Context budget retrieval
documents.body: Retrieval should return the smallest top-k document set that supports the answer. Context reduction is measured against the full corpus while answer-support terms remain covered.

documents.title: Stale derived documents
documents.body: This stale derived entry contains obsolete material and should disappear after a canonical rebuild; the old body is not authoritative.

replacement.title: Fresh source replacement
replacement.body: The current replacement body is searchable after the canonical source rebuild and the legacy body is no longer indexed.
